title: Code Review — vocabulario avanzado
description: Vocabulario y frases reales que aparecen en code reviews de equipos senior: nits, blockers, footguns, tech debt, refactors y cómo expresar disagreement de forma diplomática en comentarios de PR.

vocab.example: Nit: could we rename `data` to something more descriptive here?
Once CI is green, feel free to ship it.
LGTM, thanks for addressing the earlier comments.
Marking this as a blocker — we can't merge until the null check is added.
Small gotcha: `Date.parse` returns NaN for empty strings — worth guarding against.

vocab.translation: API peligrosa fácil de mal usar
vocab.example: This helper is a bit of a footgun — the second argument is booleans-only but the type says `any`.
What happens if the user array is empty? I think that edge case isn't covered.
There's a lot of boilerplate here — could we extract a helper?
Let's spike a proof of concept before committing to the full refactor.
I started fixing the lint config and ended up yak shaving for two hours.
Let's not bikeshed the variable name — either works, pick one and move on.
This looks like cargo cult from the old codebase — we don't need the `useMemo` here.
This is a band-aid, not a fix — let's file a follow-up for the real issue.
I know it's a kludge, but it unblocks the release — proper fix next sprint.
Nice refactor — the new structure is much easier to follow.
This file has a lot of cruft from the v1 API — worth cleaning up.
Looks like dead code — I don't see any callers of this function.
What's the `86400` here? Feels like a magic number — could we name it `SECONDS_IN_DAY`?
This function has a hidden side effect — it mutates the input array.
There's a race condition here if two requests arrive at the same time.

vocab.translation: frágil, se rompe con cambios pequeños
vocab.example: The test is brittle — it depends on the exact JSON key order.
This test has been flaky on CI all week — let's quarantine it.
The controller is tightly coupled to the DB layer — hard to unit test.
A 400-line function is a code smell — worth breaking it apart.
We're taking on tech debt here — please file a ticket to revisit next quarter.
The backend is ready — I just need to wire up the frontend form to the new endpoint.
If this goes sideways, we'll need a plan to unwind the migration.
I don't want to be gatekeeping, but this needs a security review before merge.
This is just a drive-by review — the API surface looks reasonable to me.
I think we're over-engineering this — a plain function would do.
Let's tighten up the types — `any` here defeats the purpose.
I was tearing my hair out over this bug — turned out to be a stale cache.
This PR is huge — could we split the diff into the refactor and the feature?
Let's target this for next sprint — no rush.

vocab.translation: mergear / dejar el cambio en main
vocab.example: I'd like to land this before the freeze on Friday.
Rather than revert, let's roll forward with a small patch.
Let's defer the pagination work to a follow-up PR.
I'm going to punt on the caching layer for now — file it as tech debt.

vocab.translation: seguir la conversación fuera del PR
vocab.example: Let's take this offline — happy to jump on a quick call to align.
Filed a follow-up for the accessibility work: LINGUA-482.

listening.text: This is a nit, but I'd prefer we destructure the props here for readability.
Left a blocking comment on the auth middleware — we can't ship until that's addressed.
Looks fine overall, but let's split this into two PRs: one for the refactor, one for the feature.
Small gotcha here: this only works if the array is non-empty — worth adding a guard.
I think we're over-engineering this. A plain object would do the job without the class hierarchy.
The test is flaky on CI — I'd quarantine it and file a follow-up rather than blocking the merge.
LGTM once you address the security comment. Feel free to merge after that.
Let's not bikeshed the naming — either works. Pick one and let's land the change.
This is a band-aid, not a real fix. Can we file a follow-up to address the root cause?
I'd push back on adding another dependency here — the standard library covers this case.

speaking.target: I might push back on that approach — I think the trade-off in complexity outweighs the perf gain here.
One concern is that this couples the payment logic directly to the DB — could we introduce a repository layer?
Could you help me understand why we chose polling over a webhook here? I'm probably missing context.
LGTM once you address the security comment on line 42. Feel free to merge after that lands.
I don't want to be gatekeeping, but this touches the auth path — can we get a second reviewer?
Leave a diplomatic comment asking the author to split a 1500-line PR into smaller chunks.
Approve a PR with two nits and one non-blocking suggestion, using natural code-review tone.
Politely disagree with a senior engineer's suggestion to add a caching layer, explaining your reasoning.
